# The chat is a Studio surface fed by the resolver, and the resolver still decides

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-native-chat-surface`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

Vision §63 is titled *"Do Not Put an AI Chat Into GUI/TUI"* and says, without
qualification, **"Do not embed an LLM chat as a core Gearbox feature."**
§64 says MCP is the agent interface. §111 lists `embedded AI chat` among the
explicit non-goals for V1. `cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability` sets a threshold of
*"zero language-model involvement in the correctness or explanation path"*.

A chat was nevertheless shipped. Commit `4da54a5` (2026-09-09) installed
`@theia/ai-core`, `@theia/ai-chat`, `@theia/ai-chat-ui` and `@theia/ai-anthropic`,
enabled `ai-features.AiEnable.enableAI`, added one tool, and put the widget in
the shell. No document was amended, so the repository has held a contradiction
for four days: the code does the thing the vision forbids, and neither says so.

> **Read as of 2026-09-13.** The Context below describes the state this ADR was
> written against, in the tense it was written in, and it is no longer the state
> of the repository: the decision was implemented, the chat answers, and
> `docs/conformance.md` carries six built claims for it. The paragraphs about an
> inert surface are the *reason for the decision*, not a description of today.
> This note exists because the section was read as current twice, once by its own
> author and once by someone auditing the chat four days later.

**The chat had also never worked.** `@theia/ai-chat` registers no user-facing
agent — Theia's `Universal` and `Coder` live in `@theia/ai-ide`, which this
application deliberately does not install, because it drags `puppeteer-core` and
the AI terminal surface ADR-0011 withdrew. Nothing in this repository bound a
`ChatAgent`, and no custom-agent YAML ships. Every request therefore reached
`ChatService` and came back as *"No agent was found to handle this request."*
The tool added by `4da54a5` had never been offered to a model either: a tool
reaches one only through an agent's `functions` list.

So the question is not whether to keep a working chat that contradicts the
vision. It is whether to build one at all, and if so, under what constraint —
because the surface as shipped is inert, and deleting it is as available as
finishing it.

### What §63's reasons actually object to

The section lists its reasons as a block: model/provider integration, API
credentials, streaming, conversation state, tool loops, prompt injection
surface, permissions, duplicate UX with existing developer agents.

Seven of those eight are objections to *building chat infrastructure*. Theia AI
supplies all seven — provider integration, credential handling, streaming,
session state, the tool-call loop, and the input surface — and `4da54a5` already
took that dependency. The cost §63 was avoiding is already paid, and paying it
again is not among the options.

The eighth, duplicate UX with existing developer agents, is the one that still
bites, and it is the reason §64 exists. It is also the one a native extension
answers rather than worsens: an external agent cannot see what is selected in
Studio, which profile is being shown, or which resolution produced the
diagnostics on screen. That state lives in the frontend and is not on the wire.

### What the explainability threshold actually forbids

`cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability` is the harder constraint, and it should not be
weakened to accommodate a feature.

Read precisely, it forbids a language model from *producing* a correctness
decision or an explanation. It does not forbid one from *reading aloud* an
explanation the resolver produced — and the requirement says so itself, in its
own Rationale:

> A generated justification is not evidence. **The resolver decides; a model may
> only rephrase what the resolver already recorded.**

So the permission this ADR needs is not an exception carved out of
`cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability`; it is the sentence the requirement already
ends with. Vision §70 draws the same line — `resolver decides / LLM explains` —
and names the forbidden shape as `LLM decides / LLM justifies itself`.

The requirement is therefore **not amended**. What was missing was any structural
guarantee that a chat would stay on the permitted side of its own sentence, and
that is what the rest of this decision supplies.

## Decision Drivers

* The contradiction must end. Either the code goes or the documents change; a
  repository that says one thing and does another has stopped being a
  specification.
* Explainability must not be diluted. Whatever is permitted must leave
  `cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability` true as written, not true under a new
  reading.
* No new write path. ADR-0010 made a preview mandatory in front of every write;
  a second way to change a product with a weaker gate would undo it.
* The chat must not become a second source of facts. Anything it states about a
  product must be traceable to engine output.
* MCP (§64) must remain the answer for agents outside Theia. This decision must
  not be an argument against building it.

## Considered Options

* **A — delete the chat.** Remove the four packages and the tool, restoring the
  documents' position exactly. Cheapest, and loses the live UI state that
  motivated the surface.
* **B — finish it as a general assistant.** Bind a chat agent with broad tools,
  including file access, in the manner of `@theia/ai-ide`'s `Coder`.
* **C — a domain agent with typed tools, reads only.** Bind an agent whose every
  tool returns engine output, whose previews write nothing, and whose only write
  verb is the existing previewed one.
* **D — MCP only.** Build the §64 adapter now and leave the chat inert or
  removed.

B is rejected on the explainability threshold: an agent that can read the
description as text can form its own opinion about the topology, and there is no
structural reason for it to prefer the resolver's. D is not exclusive with C and
remains planned; it does not answer the selection problem, because an external
agent cannot see the UI's state.

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen: C.** The chat becomes a native Studio surface. Vision §63 and §111 are
amended to match, and the amendment is narrow: an embedded chat is permitted
*when it is a view over the resolver*, not as a general assistant.

Four properties make the explainability threshold survive, and each is a
structural fact rather than a promise in a prompt.

### 1. Every tool returns engine output

The agent has eight read tools and no ability to read a file. Each returns what
the engine or a store already holds:

| Tool | Source |
|---|---|
| `gearbox_get_selection` | `SelectionService` |
| `gearbox_get_product` | `ResolvedProductHeader` |
| `gearbox_list_gears`, `gearbox_get_gear` | `CatalogueStore`, `ResolvedGear` |
| `gearbox_get_diagnostics` | the resolution's and catalogue's `Diagnostic`s |
| `gearbox_explain_diagnostic` | the generated catalogue (§3 below) |
| `gearbox_resolve_preview` | `gearbox/product/resolvePreview` |
| `gearbox_generate_preview` | `gearbox/generate/plan` |

There is no tool that reads `product.gdl`, a gear's Rust source, or the
filesystem. The model cannot form an independent view of the topology because it
is never given the inputs a view would be formed from — only the resolver's
conclusions. That is the enforcement: not a rule the prompt asks it to follow,
but an absence of the means to break it.

### 2. The previews are the engine's own, and write nothing

`resolvePreview` applies edits to the description in memory and resolves that;
no write gate, no lock touched. `planGenerate` is the dry run
`cpt-gearbox-fr-generate-preview` already requires. Neither is a second solver.

`applyGenerate` is deliberately **not** exposed. The only verb that changes a
product remains `gearbox_toggle_gear`, which calls `ProductEditService.toggle` —
the same entry point the catalogue's own control calls, which renders the exact
line it would write and waits for a person to agree. The chat therefore holds no
privilege the UI does not already have, which is the ADR-0010 property restated
for a new caller.

### 3. A code's meaning is generated, not recalled

`DiagnosticCode` crosses the wire as an opaque string, so nothing on the far
side could say what `GBX0410` means without an occurrence in hand. A model asked
anyway will answer confidently and sometimes wrongly, and a wrong code
explanation is indistinguishable from a right one to the person reading it.

So `crates/gearbox-ir/tests/export_diagnostics.rs` now emits a second output
beside `docs/diagnostics.md`: a TypeScript catalogue generated from the same
`DiagnosticCode::ALL`, guarded by `make diagnostics-check`. The explanation the
chat gives is the catalogue's own prose, and the two cannot drift
(`cpt-gearbox-nfr-no-type-drift`).

### 4. Context comes from the services, never the DOM

Five context variables — `#gearboxSelection`, `#gearboxProduct`,
`#gearboxDiagnostics`, `#gearboxTopology`, `#gearboxConfig` — read the same
stores that feed Catalogue, Inspector and Conflicts. Reading the rendering back
would make an answer depend on which panels happen to be open and go stale the
moment a re-resolve re-rendered underneath.

They resolve when a request is sent rather than when a chip is attached, so a
description saved on disk (`DescriptionWatchService`) or a profile switched
mid-composition is reflected rather than remembered.

Each carries a compact snapshot — identifiers and counts, with every list capped
and reporting what it omitted. Full detail arrives through tools, for the
reason the cap exists: a context window spent on the catalogue is one not spent
on the question, and a silently truncated list is worse than a short one because
the model cannot tell it was truncated.

### What this does not permit

* No general-purpose assistant, no file tools, no terminal. `@theia/ai-ide`
  stays uninstalled.
* No write that skips the preview.
* No claim about a product that did not come from a tool call.
* No LLM in the engine, the CLI, or any test's assertion path.

## Consequences

Good:

* The chat answers at all, which it did not before.
* The contradiction between the code and the documents is closed in one
  direction, explicitly, with the narrower permission written down.
* A code's meaning becomes readable outside Rust for the first time, which
  serves the Inspector and any future client as much as the chat.
* `cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability` is now enforced by the shape of the tool
  surface rather than by nobody having tried.

Bad, or at least owed:

* A surface exists that a prompt injection can reach. It can read the product and
  propose changes; it cannot write without a person agreeing, which bounds the
  damage to what a person would approve on a diff they were shown.
* An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the backend environment is now load-bearing for a
  visible feature rather than an inert one. Absent, the agent registers and
  every request fails at model selection.
* **And the environment is the only way to supply it.** Not installing
  `@theia/ai-ide` (ADR-0011, for `puppeteer-core` and the AI terminal) also
  withholds the AI Configuration view: `@theia/ai-core-ui` registers no view of
  its own, so the settings page's "AI settings have moved to the AI
  Configuration view" points at a view this application does not have. The
  preference `ai-features.anthropic.AnthropicApiKey` is still registered -- and
  therefore still read -- but it is not reachable either: searching the settings
  editor for "Anthropic" returns *No Settings Found*, because Theia 1.75 hides
  the AI preferences from that editor in favour of the view. So the key can be
  supplied in exactly two ways, neither of them a user interface: the backend's
  environment, or hand-editing `settings.json`, which stores it in clear text.
  While the chat was inert this cost nothing; making it work made it a real gap.

  **Closed by ADR-0011's amendment of 2026-09-14.** Studio contributes a
  `gearbox.ai.apiKey` preference and a *Gearbox* section in the ordinary settings
  editor -- possible because the filter that hides the AI keys matches
  `ai-features.` by literal prefix. The `ai-ide` exclusion stands; the editor is
  reused rather than rebuilt. The key is still clear text in the user's settings
  file, and the setting says so.

  The failure a person met, *"Couldn't find a ready language model for agent
  Gearbox"*, is likewise replaced: the agent now checks readiness before the
  request and answers in the product's own words, naming the setting and the
  environment variable.
* Theia asks the operator to confirm every tool call by default. The eight read
  tools are pre-approved in the application's frontend configuration and the
  write verb deliberately is not. The asymmetry is this decision made
  operational: a dialog in front of a harmless read teaches people to click
  through dialogs, and the write gate depends on them not having that habit.
* §64's MCP adapter is still unbuilt, and this decision makes it *less* urgent
  while leaving it just as necessary for `cpt-gearbox-actor-external-agent`.

## Confirmation

* `ide/tests/conformance/adr-0017-native-chat.spec.ts` — six claims: that the
  chat offers a `Gearbox` agent at all, that selecting a gear names it on a
  single chip, that the chip follows the selection rather than accumulating, that
  a selection made before the chat opened still produces a chip, and that a
  catalogue row and a conflict row are both draggable.
* `make diagnostics-check` — the generated catalogue cannot fall behind the
  declaration it is generated from, and a first-ever generated file cannot pass
  while being absent from the commit.
* `crates/gearbox-ir/tests/export_diagnostics.rs` — `every_code_reaches_studio`
  and `ts_export_is_deterministic`, beside the existing pair for the Markdown
  reference.

**What a live pass established, outside the suite.** Against a real model the
agent chained `get_selection`, `get_product`, `get_diagnostics`, `get_gear` and
`resolve_preview` unprompted, and answered a profile question from the
resolver's output rather than from its own reading. It declined twice to say
what a diagnostic code means without calling `explain_diagnostic` first, which
is the rule in §3 holding under its own weight. The pass also found a defect in
this decision's own tooling: `get_gear` reported inclusion as a bare
`in_product` boolean, which is false for a plugin the description declares for
another profile, and the agent faithfully repeated it. The tool now passes on
the resolver's `selected_by` reasons and the intent's plugin declarations
instead of summarising them.

**What is not asserted by a test, and why.** No test checks what the agent
*says*: that needs a key and a network, and a second run would not agree with
the first — a suite whose result depends on a sampler has reported nothing.

Nor is "no tool can write" asserted through the browser, because the only way to
observe it would be to ask a model to try. It is instead a property of the
source: `gearbox-tools.ts` declares eight handlers, none of which calls
`applyGenerate` or touches the filesystem, and the agent's `functions` list names
exactly those eight plus the previewed write verb. Adding a writing tool is a
visible edit to that list, which is a weaker guarantee than a failing test and
should be read as one.

## Traceability

* Amends vision §63 and §111 (`docs/vision.md`), which forbade
  this outright.
* Applies vision §70's `resolver decides / LLM explains` as the governing rule,
  and §67's proposal model as the shape of every write.
* Leaves `cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability` (`docs/PRD.md`) **unamended** and true
  as written. Its Rationale already permits a model to "rephrase what the
  resolver already recorded"; this decision supplies the structural guarantee
  that it can do nothing else, by withholding the inputs an independent
  explanation would need.
* Introduces `cpt-gearbox-fr-chat-context` (`docs/PRD.md` §5.4), and the matching
  §4.2 exclusion that keeps a general-purpose assistant out of scope.
* Serves `cpt-gearbox-fr-explain`: the explanation graph gains a reader that can
  be asked questions in words.
* Reuses `cpt-gearbox-fr-generate-preview` unchanged as the generation tool, and
  respects `cpt-gearbox-fr-rpc-writes-opt-in` by adding no new writing method.
* Obeys ADR-0010: the one write verb is the previewed one, and the tool holds no
  policy of its own.
* Depends on ADR-0011 for the shell it sits in, and inherits that ADR's reason
  for not installing `@theia/ai-ide`.
* Applies `cpt-gearbox-nfr-no-type-drift` to Studio's view of the diagnostic
  catalogue, as `make grammar-check` applies it to the editor's view of the
  language, and as ADR-0015 applies it to the documents' view.
* Does not supersede vision §64. MCP remains the interface for
  `cpt-gearbox-actor-external-agent`; this serves
  `cpt-gearbox-actor-theia-studio`, whose state is not on the wire.

## Amendment 2026-09-16: the decision landed, and the key has a second home

**Status: accepted. This records what shipped; it reverses nothing.**

The Decision Outcome above is implemented. `GearboxChatAgent` is bound as the
`ChatAgent`, the default and the fallback agent id, so a plain sentence resolves
to it; the eight read tools and the one write verb are offered through its
`functions`; and `docs/conformance.md` carries six built claims for the surface.

Three things are true now that the text above predates:

* **The key is a setting first.** ADR-0011's 2026-09-14 amendment added
  `gearbox.ai.apiKey`, and it takes precedence; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the
  backend's environment is the fallback, and `npm run start:browser` loads a
  `.env` at the repository root into it. The Consequences above say the variable
  is "load-bearing", which was true when only it existed.
* **A refusal at the transport now says what it was.** The Anthropic SDK reports
  any rejected request as `APIConnectionError`, whose default message is the bare
  string `Connection error.`, and Theia's error codec was dropping the engine's
  own diagnostics on the way to the browser besides. `Gearbox: Check AI
  Connection` probes the provider from the backend with no key -- any status,
  401 included, means the transport works -- and the chat reports the cause chain
  instead of the bare string.
* **The two ways to break the trust store are documented**, because both present
  as that same string: `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca` on a Node whose bundled
  OpenSSL has no CA store configured, and `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing at a single
  corporate root, which on Node >= 22 replaces the store rather than extending
  it. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is the one that appends. The launcher detects the
  first and warns about the second.

Still unbuilt, and still correctly listed above: the MCP adapter of vision §64,
and the AI Configuration view that `@theia/ai-ide` would bring.
